problem: Given that the tangent line approximation to the function $f(x)$ at $x=-3$ underestimates the values of the function in the neighborhood of $x=-3,$ which of the following must be true?

choices.value: $f(x)$ is concave up in the neighborhood of $x=-3$
$f(x)$ is concave down in the neighborhood of $x=-3$

activity_context.topic_title: Approximating Functions Using Local Linearity and Linearization

examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Tangent Line Approximation and Classifying it as an Underestimate or Overestimate
examples.problem: The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ passes through $(-2,-5)$ and is concave down on the interval $(-\infty,0).$ If $f'(-2)=3$, estimate the value of $f(-2.3)$ using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=-2$ and determine whether the approximation is an underestimate or overestimate.
examples.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation to $f(x)$ at the point $a=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(-2)+{f}^{′}(-2)(x-(-2)) \\  & =f(-2)+{f}^{′}(-2)(x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

The function passes through the point $(-2,-5),$ so we have $f(-2)=-5.$ Also, we're told that $f'(-2)=3,$ so we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =-5+3(x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(-2.3)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=-2.3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2.3) & ≈L(-2.3) \\  & =-5+3(-2.3+2) \\  & =-5+3(-0.3) \\  & =-5-0.9 \\  & =-5.9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the function is concave down on the interval $(-\infty,0)$, the linear approximation $L(x)$ is above the graph near $x=-2,$ and therefore we have an overestimate.

feedback.problem: Let $f$ be a function such that ${f}^{′}(x)=(5x-3)^{2}(4x-2)^{4}$ and $f(0)=3.$ Use the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=0$ to estimate the value of $f(2).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)(x-0) \\  & =f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)x\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $f(0)=3,$ and since ${f}^{′}(x)=(5x-3)^{2}(4x-2)^{4},$ then ${f}^{′}(0)=(5(0)-3)^{2}(4(0)-2)^{4}=144.$ So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
L(x)=3+144x.
$$

Now, we can approximate $f(2)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=2.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) & ≈L(2) \\  & =3+144(2) \\  & =3+288 \\  & =291.\end{aligned}
$$
